question.text: This man served as president of Princeton from 1902 to 1910 before being elected U.S. president in 1912.
question.clue: This president's secretary of state resigned after the sinking of the Lusitania.

swap.text: This American feminist, who was featured on the dollar coin, worked alongside Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucy Stone to create the National American Woman Suffrage Association.
swap.clue: Carrie Chapman Catt succeeded this Quaker in one post, and after this figure was barred from speaking at an Albany temperance meeting, she formed the Woman's New York State Temperance Society.

question.text: Washington was invited by this President, who took office after the death of William McKinley. In his military career, this man fought with the "Buffalo Soldiers" as leader of the Rough Riders.
question.clue: This president summarized his foreign policy, "Speak softly and carry a big stick."

swap.leadin: Answer the following about scandals in American presidential history.
swap.text: This scandal during the Harding administration dealt with the fixing of oil prices and saw the Secretary of the Interior, Albert Fall, convicted of conspiracy and bribery.
swap.clue: John Kendrick began the investigation of this event, which acquitted Edwin Denby but implicated other members of the Ohio Gang.

question.text: Wilson had earlier beaten this Republican candidate in the 1916 election. Due to their similarly progressive records as governors, Theodore Roosevelt quipped that the only difference between the two men "was a shave".
question.clue: He replaced Bainbridge Colby as Secretary of State and chaired the Washington Naval Conference.

swap.leadin: This man's Secretary of State, Philander Knox, pursued a policy of "dollar diplomacy" with regards to Latin America.
swap.text: Name this president who claimed that the Payne-Aldrich tariff was the "best tariff bill ever passed" in his Winona Speech. He later served as Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.
swap.clue: The policy of giving loans to Banana Republics in South America, known as "Dollar Diplomacy" was established under this president.

question.text: Czolgosz was inspired to support anarchism after hearing this woman speak in Cleveland. Although she did not condone his assassination of William McKinley, she asked, "Who knows but what he, too, was willing to 'fight for his country and die for her liberty?'" in her defense of Czolgosz.
question.clue: She was boycotted by the British left after discussing her horror with Leninism in My Disillusionment in Russia, and her other writings include the periodical Mother Earth.

swap.leadin: Alexander Hamilton helped Morgan Lewis win this position.
swap.text: Name this position. Lewis' predecessor, George Clinton, spent over twenty years holding this position, which would also be held by his nephew DeWitt.
swap.clue: During his tenure in this office, Nelson Rockefeller called in the National Guard to suppress a riot at the Attica Prison.

question.leadin: BONUS. Name these labor cases brought before the Supreme Court.
question.text: Justice Peckham wrote that a state law limiting the workweek of bakers violated the freedom of contract in this 1905 case.
question.clue: The argument that the Fourteenth Amendment does not "enact" Spencer's Social Statics was put forth in Holmes's dissent.

swap.text: The overthrow of Jose Santos Zelaya's regime in Nicaragua was a chief effect of this policy formulated by Philander Knox. For 15 points, name this Taft Administration program that used loans in an attempt to influence Latin American governments.
swap.clue: Its failures became clear when Nicaragua's populace, on grounds of national dignity, refused to support a loan request from Zelaya's successor, showing that it cannot account for non-economic motivators.

question.text: A 2017 book by Elizabeth Cobbs documented a group of women switchboard operators, like Merle Egan, who were specifically chosen to serve in World War I by this commander of the American Expeditionary Forces.
question.answerHtml: John Pershing [or John Joseph Pershing; accept Black Jack Pershing; prompt on Black Jack] (Cobbs’book is The Hello Girls.)
question.clue: After the Battle of Columbus, Woodrow Wilson tapped this general to defeat Pancho Villa.

swap.text: In the 1924 election, Coolidge ran against the unpopular Republican John Davis and this popular Progressive candidate, who had earlier lost the 1912 election to Roosevelt.
swap.clue: His first bid for President came in 1912, when he won the North Dakota primary but failed to secure the Republican nomination.

question.text: Eugenicists supported this decision upholding a 1927 Virginia law allowing forced sterilization. Oliver Wendell Holmes stated, "three generations of imbeciles are enough" in this case against John Bell.
question.clue: This case focused on a woman who was raped by a relative and whose mother was alleged to have had a history of prostitution and immorality.

swap.leadin: Name some losing American presidential candidates.
swap.text: When he wasn't in jail, for example in violation of the Espionage Act in 1918, he was the usual candidate for the Socialist Party from 1904-1920.
swap.clue: This man later helped found a political party on whose ticket he ran five times.

question.text: This most successful American fighter ace during World War One, was a character witness in Billy Mitchell's court martial. This CEO of Eastern Air Lines visited Russia during World War Two to study the Soviet air force.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about United States involvement with Cuba.
swap.text: This 1901 amendment to the Cuban constitution, inserted at the behest of the U.S., bound Cuba to lease the Guantanamo base to the U.S. and avoid compromising its independence.
swap.clue: This legislation prohibited a certain entity from entering into debt that it could not pay, or from making territorial concessions to anybody except the United States.

question.text: The Pollock case resulted in the eventual passage and ratification of this law, which according to chief proponent Nebraska Senator Norris Brown "cannot be interpreted in two ways." It legalized the income tax.
question.clue: It became necessary after the Court's ruling in Pollock v. Farmer's Loan and Trust Company, even though the Court had earlier allowed a three percent levy to help finance the Civil War.

swap.text: Domestically, support for Kellogg-Briand was led by this man, then Chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.

question.leadin: According to the attorney Buck Colbert Franklin, flaming turpentine balls were dropped on buildings in this neighborhood during one event that took place here.
question.text: Name this affluent neighborhood, dubbed the "Black Wall Street," which was destroyed in 1921 by a mob after an elevator operator alleged that she was assaulted by the shoeshiner Dick Rowland.

swap.leadin: This man spent six years working as a wood-cutter in Germany.
swap.text: Name this man elected mayor of Milwaukee in 1910. He was the first Socialist mayor elected to lead a major American city.
swap.clue: The Sewer Socialists elected this man mayor of Milwaukee in 1910. He was the first Socialist mayor in American history and was Eugene Debs's running mate in 1912.
